steps.text: 10:21 A.M. Rhodes Island Training Ground

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: This is it!

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Too slow!

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Shit!

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: But...!

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: That's enough for today.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Phew....

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Not bad, Fang. You blocked it this time.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: I'm glad to see you getting more flexible.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Yeah, it's what Instructor Dobermann taught me. Not just about footwork, but about adjusting my speed. I think I'm starting to get the hang of it!

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Right. You have your natural Kuranta speed. It's good for quick attacks, but those aren't worth anything if the enemy blocks them and you have no counter.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Anyway, you passed this field exercise.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Thanks, Instructor Grace!

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: But the next one will be even harder.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I'll be ready!

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: That's the spirit.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Fang~

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Beagle, did you finish your test? How did it go?

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Aw, I didn't pass.... Instructor Fallon has some real sneaky tricks...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Don't get discouraged. You'll get 'em next time.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: How about you? Did you pass?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Nice...

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Aww, my butt...

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Kroos, are you okay?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Instructor Tess shot my patootie...

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: The test was a sniper war between me and Instructor Tess. We had to hide and find each other. I still don't know how she got behind me!

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Hahahahahaha!

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Don't laugh at me, Uncle Grace!

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: I'll tell you, you got really unlucky. The other sniping instructors just happen to be out for a few days and you got stuck with Tess.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Even I can't keep track of that phantom. My advice is you put the same effort into finding a sniper nest that you do into finding places to nap.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Yeah, yeah. Laugh it up.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: I just checked on Hibiscus and Lava. Lava passed, but Hibiscus didn't. They went home already. How did you do?

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Fang passed.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Aw, Fang, you traitor!

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Why am I a traitor?

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Ugh, I failed again. What is wrong with me...?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Don't be discouraged, Beagle, we still have plenty of chances.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Yeah, it's just a quiz. Nothing to be too upset about. And we still have hell this afternoon.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Haha, that's right. Dobermann let us do your individual tests this morning. But the afternoon group field test? That's all her.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: *Sigh* Please. I can already imagine the look on Instructor Dobermann's face when she sees my test results.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Now you're sorry?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: No. Instructor Dobermann said we could go at our own pace. I'm just a late bloomer!

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Hah hah.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: But I'm also worried she'll be disappointed in us...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Beagle, Kroos.....

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Okay, seriously, don't be too hard on yourselves. We didn't make these tests so you could pass them. They're there to tell us what to work on.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Wow. It feels awful when a guy tells you straight to your face that he's better than you. And you can't even do anything about it!

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: It's the truth. There's a huge skill gap between you trainees and us instructors.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: That's why we're your teachers. That's what we're here for.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: And even if you haven't noticed it yourselves, you've made huge strides since you came to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: ...He's right.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Yeah... I guess he is.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: And really, you girls are doing great. The instructors you went up against are all experts in your respective fields.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Do you have any idea how we got where we are? What we've been through?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: No way...

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Yes. Dobermann alone trained us.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Hard to believe as it may be, Dobermann today is a hundred times softer than she used to be.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Huh? Are we talking about the same Dobermann? She's soft?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: That's not funny, Uncle Grace.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: I'm not kidding.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Grace! My abuela runs up a mountain with a pack twice that size! You really can't handle some light jogging?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Fallon, you want the enemy to die laughing? Is that what you're going for with these clumsy slapstick attacks?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Tess, you falling asleep on me? Hold your gun straight! Don't let me out of your sights!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Viktor, the enemy doesn't give water breaks!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Leah, let's have you learn some basic first aid before you try healing Arts. This bandage work is as much of a mess as you are.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: We're done for the day. Give me ten laps around the training room! You hear me?

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: Sir, yes, sir!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: I can't hear you!

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: SIR, YES, SIR!

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: That bad, huh?

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: The point is still that Dobermann may not be the strongest fighter herself.... Hey, I'll toot my own horn and say I've got a 50/50 shot against her at this point.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Come on, cut the crap.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Hey, a little self-confidence is good for the soul.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Anyway, Dobermann may not be the strongest fighter around, but the tactics and strategies she pulled out of her time with the Bolívarian army are overpowering.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Bolívar....?

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Yeah. Like the 'Bolívarian Civil War' you see on the news. That Bolívar. We all wonder exactly how Dobermann got to be as great as she is, but she never talks that much about her time in Bolívar.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Anyway, at the time, Rhodes Island was just getting going, and they really needed some talent. Then, how do I put this...

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Dobermann was a real soldier back then.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: What does that mean?

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Like, we're all pretty awesome here at Rhodes Island, but our overall atmosphere is still really relaxed, right? We get to have our own lives.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Okay, let me put it this way. If you were with us back then, Kroos, you'd never end up napping in a utility closet. The thought wouldn't even cross your mind.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Huh? That sounds like hell.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: You get what I'm saying? Dobermann's way different now.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Really. It's hard to imagine the person Instructor Grace is talking about is our Instructor Dobermann.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Yeah... Dobermann works us hard, and she's kind of scary, but once you get to know her, you can tell she really cares about us.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: She always really cared about people. Even back then.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: It's just, sometimes, what you do means more than why you do it.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: All right, that's enough chatting for now. You girls pack up, go take a shower, have lunch, and get ready for the group training this afternoon.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Me? I'm going to gather up the other teachers and we'll take your test results to Dobermann.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Oh, I can do that for you.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Really? You can?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Sure. We'll pass Instructor Dobermann's room on the way to the cafeteria.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Oh. I'll go too.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Um, I'll pass. I'm in no hurry to see Instructor Dobermann.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Thanks a lot, ladies.

steps.name: Instructor Grace
steps.text: Oh, and uh, don't tell Dobermann what I just told you. Ever.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Instructor Dobermann!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Oh? What are you two doing here?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: We're bringing you some test results, and I guess some other information from Instructor Grace.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I passed!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Let's see here... Oh, good.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: The others.... Kroos, Beagle, and Hibiscus didn't pass. Did Lava?

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Sorry....

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: It's okay, you're making progress.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Go on back and tell Kroos to be ready for this afternoon.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Ahahahaha.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Go on. Rest up.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Okay!

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Hey, Instructor Dobermann, are you cleaning your room?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Yes. I do so regularly.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Can I help you?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Huh? Why?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Um. Sometimes you want to give back to your teacher, you know?

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Oh, I'll help too!

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Er, unless we'd get in the way?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: ...No, not at all. I'm just a little surprised. I thought you were scared of me.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: No way! I have a lot of respect for you, Instructor.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Me too!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: All right. I'll take the help. Thanks.

steps.name: Fang & Beagle
steps.text: Okay!

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: There's a lot more stuff in here than I expected...

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Oh? Is that odd?

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: No. I just always thought of you as an instructor with a tidy room, the type who wouldn't keep a lot of stuff.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: ....I really didn't bring much with me when I first came to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: But I've been living here for a few years now.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Oh, right. Instructor Dobermann joined Rhodes Island a long time ago?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Yes, compared to most operators. It's been a while.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Why did you join up, Instructor?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Oh, sorry. Is that a bad question?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: No. It's just, now's not the time. We'll talk about it later.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Are you curious too?

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Eh? Yes... I am! I really want to know more about you, Instructor.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Know more about me... huh?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Might as well start on the wardrobe...

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Hey, Instructor Dobermann, is this a uniform?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Huh? Yes.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: It's a souvenir I kept from my time in the Army.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Wow, it's very cool.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: It is.... So which side did you fight on?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: You know a bit about Bolívar, huh?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: And don't I remember that Beagle is also of Bolívarian origin? You immigrated to Columbia, is that right?

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Yes, but I've only heard about Bolívar from my parents. I'd love to hear more about it.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Oh, but it's not like I just came because...

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Relax. Even if you did, it's okay.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Come help me with the bedding.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Okay!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: There we go. Thanks.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: There are currently three factions in Bolívar. The nominal, official government is a puppet controlled by Leithanien, since they led the forces that won the war against Columbia.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Then the Autonomous Government resulted from a parliamentary split. They've been looking for a chance to seize power. They're well-funded, and offer a challenge to the puppet government.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Last, we have the Bolívarian Resistance, an uprising made up of ordinary people fed up with the struggles of the powerful.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: I served the Autonomous Government, at the rank of colonel.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Wow, a colonel! Instructor Dobermann is awesome!

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: That's a high rank.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: .....Yes. It is.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: I'll wipe down the top of the wardrobe. There must be lots of dust up there.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Aaahh——choo!

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Oops, something fell down?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: It's... a bunch of metal tags?

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: These are.... name plates.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Name plates? Like the ID cards we have at Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Yes. Soldiers in the army get these plates issued with their name and unit number, for identification.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Ah, really.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Can I see them?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Take a look.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: A... lan. Ju..... an. Jo.... se. I can read the names, but I can't make sense of these abbreviations...

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Those indicate some things about the units they served in. Don't worry about them.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: If you have their name plates, does that mean they're...

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Yes. They're all dead.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Oh. So, were, were they important people to you?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Important...?
Colonel, your men died bravely.
Don't grieve for them. Their deaths have saved my career, and yours. You won't be reprimanded by the brass.
An investigation? No one will remember these things.
The truth? Colonel, people need pretty, or at least decent results. They don't care about the truth.
Colonel, remember your place. And don't forget who it was who raised you up from a common soldier to the command you hold today!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: I didn't know them well. We barely spoke.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: But yes. They are important to me.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: ........We're just about done cleaning. Come here.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Um, did I do something wrong, Instructor?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: No. I wasn't trying to hide them. That's why they were just kind of left up there.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: But your questions got me thinking. So I want to talk to you two.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Oh, well, I'm honored!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Relax. Just have a seat.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: I will tell you about my past at some point, but not now.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: For now, I just want to ask you a question.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: What do you think is the defining characteristic of a soldier?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Ah? Is this... a test?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: No. There are no wrong answers.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Phew.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Let's see, um.... combat proficiency?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Most people learn to fight. The operators here all do, and you two will. It's not something unique.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Is it being able to use some kind of awesome weapon?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: It's true that many manufactured weapons are readily accessible to the military....

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: But as you've seen here at Rhodes Island, there's always people who have other ways of acquiring such things.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: There's a lot of them?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Yes.... That is a big one, the military usually has a numerical advantage unmatched by civilian organizations.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Rhodes Island today can only compare the standing army of maybe a backwater nomadic city in a small country.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Whaa? I thought Rhodes Island was really powerful...

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: For a non-governmental organization, Rhodes Island has done very well for itself. But we couldn't dream of challenging a state.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: But we have such amazing operators. Like Skyfire, she goes 'swoosh' with her staff and everything goes 'fwoom!'

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: But there's only so much you can do in the face of an overwhelming numbers.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Do you remember Gus, from the garrison? He was the toughest guy there by far, but if a dozen men ganged up on him...

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Exactly. Numbers change the calculation even for a mediocre combatant. One Beagle couldn't take on Skyfire. But what about ten, or a hundred Beagles? Think about it.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: A- a hundred mes? We- we could crush Skyfire...

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Sorry, Skyfire....

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Heh. Exactly. The number of times a lone individual has used her individual strength to influence warfare on a national scale is zero. In the entire recorded history of human conflict.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Anyway.... To digress a little, there's a reason I haven't been systematically explaining the Army to you in your prep courses. There's just no value to it.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: My greatest hope is that you'll never have a chance to apply any of this knowledge. This little lesson here is completely voluntary.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: So numbers aren't the answer either?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Well, it's an answer, but it's more of a descriptor of the military itself, rather than a soldier.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Hmmm....

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Um. Is it following orders?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: What makes you say that?

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: I just thought back to our time at the garrison. The captain said that as a soldier, you have to follow orders no matter what.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Huh? I got it right!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: You did. The defining characteristic of a soldier is obedience to the chain of command.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: There's a saying: the best soldier is one who can't think. An army does not need soldiers to think. Only to follow orders.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: But isn't that kind of cruel?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: War is cruel. And if you must engage in it, giving up thought could be a kind of relief.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: But....

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Isn't it cruel that you have these questions at all? Aren't soldiers human?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Obviously, a soldier is not a machine. He comes closer to death than anyone, and he knows better than anyone exactly what it is he is facing.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Can a soldier still muster up morale when he knows he's carrying out an incredibly stupid order?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I think... no?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Of course not. So when faced with such a situation, you have two choices. Do you know what they are?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: One is to prevent the soldier from noticing the order is incredibly stupid.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: But that's difficult. The men on the front lines know exactly what kind of danger they are facing. You can't fool them.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: If you could, you could've made a better choice.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: And that other choice is to just issue the correct orders.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: It may sound a bit silly, but it's the truth. How else do you get a soldier to surrender his inclination to question orders?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: How do you get him to relax, and trust in his command?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: It's simple. Just issue convincing, correct orders from the beginning.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: But not everyone makes the right choice.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: After leaving the Autonomous Government, I moved to join the Resistance. But in the end I left. Because it wasn't any different there.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Woah. Instructor Dobermann even joined the Resistance?!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Yes. There's a picture in the second drawer under the wardrobe. Take a look

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Wowww. You looked so cool back then, Instructor.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I wanna see!

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Woah. She did!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Put it back when you're done.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Things didn't go well there either. And eventually I left Bolívar and came to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: My expectations were low.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: But I was pleasantly surprised.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: A soldier knows when he's been given a stupid order, but he may not know what to do about it.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: That's another reason you need the right orders.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: And Rhodes Island provides those.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: (whispering) Fang, do you get what she's talking about?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: (whispering) Kinda...

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Don't worry about it too much. It's just me waxing philosophical.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: The main point here is you could stand to appreciate Rhodes Island a bit more.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: You can safely give yourselves to Rhodes Island. Even if you don't think about what you're fighting for, you won't lose anything.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: There's an age old question: If we know we have to move forward, but forward is always in front of us, how do we know which way to move?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: There's no answer to that question. But you can at least trust in Rhodes Island when they tell you which way is forward. You can't go wrong moving that way.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Trust in Rhodes Island.... I think... I think I get what you're trying to tell us.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Yeah. Basically, Rhodes Island is a good place?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: ........Heh heh. Yeah. That's about it.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: It's an pie-in-the-sky paradise that a few idealists are desperately trying to keep going, for the sake of a little hope.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: I know Rhodes Island is good... But is it really that good...?

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Heh heh. It might take a while for you girls to realize it.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: All right, that's enough cleaning and chattering. It's time for you two to get some chow.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Ah! Oh no! It's almost 1!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Yep. Thanks for helping me clean up. You have something to eat. I'll be right along.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: Okay, thanks for the lesson, Instructor Dobermann. I need some time to digest it.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Me too!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Don't take it too seriously.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Also, I changed my mind. I think I might put this on one of my tests.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: And if you two feed me back exactly what I just said, you get a zero.

steps.name: Beagle
steps.text: Aaaaagh! No way!

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: I- I'll think very carefully about it! Thanks again for your lesson today, Instructor!

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Instructor, huh.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Somehow, I'm getting used to teaching.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: I've had many students, some of whom have long surpassed me. And others have bright futures.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: I've found a new purpose in Rhodes Island. And I'm willing to believe in the future that Amiya and Dr. Kal'tsit have painted for me, but....

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Alan.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Juan.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Jose.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: My roots are still in Bolívar.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: I'll go back, someday, and see for myself.

steps.name: Dobermann
steps.text: Someday.
